2026-11-26.title: Fourth Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Here we have no lasting city
Rejoice that your names are written in heaven
2026-11-26.verse: Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
theo: “For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.” Hebrews reminds us that the Church is a pilgrim people; our true citizenship is in heaven. Meanwhile we offer “a sacrifice of praise to God… the fruit of lips that confess his name,” and do not neglect to do good and share.

The seventy-two return rejoicing at their success; Jesus redirects their joy: rejoice that your names are written in heaven. Then he himself rejoices in the Holy Spirit and thanks the Father for revealing these things to infants. True joy is not in what we achieve but in belonging to God.
outline: Ask: what makes you happiest: success, or belonging to God?
We are pilgrims on the way to the city to come.
Our deepest joy is being known and loved by God.
God shows himself to the humble.
live: Praise God aloud for five minutes today.
Share a meal or gift with someone in need.
2026-11-26.prayer: Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I praise you because you reveal yourself to the little ones. Write my name in heaven and keep me a faithful pilgrim toward the city to come. Amen.

2026-11-26.question: Where do I look for my joy?

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews says: here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come (Hebrews 13:14). The Church is a pilgrim people; our true citizenship is in heaven. Meanwhile we offer God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess his name, and we do not neglect to do good and to share what we have (Hebrews 13:15–16).

The seventy-two return from their mission full of joy: Lord, in your name even the demons submit to us. Jesus says: rejoice that your names are written in heaven. At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit: I thank you, Father, because you have revealed these things to infants (Luke 10:17–21).
Pilgrims travel light and keep a joyful heart. Our joy is not in our successes, but in the fact that God knows us. Today let us sing a hymn of praise, and share what we have with someone. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says your names are written in heaven. How wonderful! Sing a song to Jesus today.

intro: Pilgrims without a lasting city, rejoicing that they belong to God.

sub: Abraham lived in tents looking for the city with foundations.
The Church walks toward the heavenly city.
q: Then Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “Surely the LORD is in this place—and I did not know it!”
Nevertheless, do not rejoice at this, that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

sub: He thanks the Father for the little ones.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you.

At that same hour Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the intelligent and have revealed them to infants.”
points.apply: Thank God for one simple person who taught you faith.

sub: Praise and sharing are the Christian's sacrifices.
The Qurbana is the great sacrifice of praise.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering.
He said to them, “I watched Satan fall from heaven like a flash of lightning.”
points.apply: Praise God aloud for five minutes today.

concl: Our joy is that God knows our names.
Let us praise him and share with others.
2026-11-26.resolve: End each day this week with a prayer of praise.
